methods.label: Substitute the intersection coordinates
methods.explanation:
The intersection point lies on both lines, so \(x=1\) and \(y=2\) must satisfy both equations. Substitution gives
\[
1=\frac14(2)+a,
\qquad
2=\frac14(1)+b.
\]
Subtracting the known term in each equation yields
\[
a=\frac12,
\qquad
b=\frac74.
\]
Therefore
\[
a+b=\frac12+\frac74=\frac94,
\]
which is choice E.
